root_cause.text: In vrealloc_node_align(), when a reallocation is forced due to NUMA node or alignment constraints, the memcpy() used the original object size (old_size) as the copy length without bounding it to the new allocation size (size), causing an out-of-bounds write when shrinking.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "On this path (need_realloc), the code allocates a new object of 'size' bytes and then memcpy()s 'old_size' bytes into it. If the request is to shrink the object (size < old_size), this results in an out-of-bounds write on the new buffer." The patch changes the memcpy to use `min(size, old_size)` as the copy length.
